steps: This video shows how structured outputs replace fragile text parsing. Without a schema, the agent answers your code in prose, and your code is left trying to regex the amount out of free text.
So instead, your code calls query with an output format: a J S O N schema of exactly three fields, vendor, amount and due date. The agent now knows the shape its answer must take.
The prompt says extract the fields from invoice dot t x t, so the agent uses the Read tool, the only tool it is allowed, and the invoice text comes back.

The agent produces its J S O N object, vendor Acme, amount twelve hundred and fifty, and it validates against the schema. If it kept failing, you would get a max structured output retries error instead.
The validated object arrives in the result message as structured output. It is already a dictionary, not a string, and the run ends with a success subtype.

Typed data just works. Your code adds ten percent tax, giving thirteen hundred and seventy five, and writes one clean typed row to the database. Schemas replace scraping. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
